newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's real rises 0.26 pct in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's real rises 0.26 pct in speculative trade.

text.p: Brazil's real closed up 0.26 percent at 1.0258 per greenback in speculative trading on the commercial foreign exchange market, dealers said.

Banks speculated early in the day over continued dollar outflows, trading the local currency between 1.0275 and 1.0285 per dollar at the open. On Tuesday, net dollar flows posted a $61.4 million deficit.

The real recovered some ground as net dollar flows pointed to a surplus today. Preliminary figures for commercial and financial foreign exchange contracts showed a Wednesday surplus of $100 million, dealers said.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real ended at 1.0312 per dollar, down 0.04 percent.
In the illegal parallel market, the real fell 1.30 percent to close at 1.092 real per greenback.
The real's fall in the black market was caused by a continued reduction in the supply of dollars, traders said.
"The supply dropped because the dollar inflows in the black market were down and those who have dollars have not been selling them lately," one trader said.
